description: Early Warning Information Increases Options for Drought Mitigation is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by University of Wisconsin-Madison | Cooperative Institute for Meteorological Satellite Studies; National Drought Mitigation Center; University of Oklahoma. In the growing season, farmers and ranchers keep a watchful eye for any sign of drought. Early warning information can increase their range of options for dealing with the lack of water. Coverage: the United States (2015). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
